milestone: Iran declares the Natanz pilot (PFEP) and commercial (FEP) enrichment plants to the Agency during the Director General's visit
UF6 first introduced into a centrifuge at Natanz PFEP (single machine test); ten-machine cascade tested with UF6 from 19 Aug 2003
Iran suspends all enrichment related and reprocessing activities
Iran removes Agency seals at Natanz (10-11 Jan 2006), ending the suspension of enrichment R&D
Enrichment to 3.6% U-235 at Natanz PFEP (164-machine cascade), declared by Iran; Agency samples of 18 Apr 2006 tend to confirm

First UF6 fed into cascades at Natanz FEP (between 17 Feb 2007, when none had been fed per GOV/2007/8 para 10, and the end of February: 'since the beginning of operations in February 2007', GOV/2008/4 para 43)
Natanz FEP producing LEU: Iran declares enrichment up to 4.8% U-235; eight 164-machine cascades being fed on 13 May 2007
First FEP product quantified: about 75 kg UF6 at stated 3.8% U-235 at the first physical inventory taking
First UF6 fed to a new-generation centrifuge: single IR-2 at PFEP (0.8 kg, 22-27 Jan 2008); 10-machine IR-2 cascade installed
First UF6 fed to a 10-machine IR-2 cascade at PFEP (period 28 Jan-16 May 2008)
FEP LEU product verified by the Agency at 3.49% U-235 (839 kg UF6 produced to 17 Nov 2008)
First UF6 fed to single IR-2m ('IR-2 modified') and IR-4 centrifuges, and to a 10-machine IR-3 cascade, at PFEP (period 15 Jan-23 May 2009)
First UF6 fed to 10-machine IR-2m and IR-4 cascades at PFEP (period 24 May-13 Aug 2009)
Iran informs the Agency by letter that it has decided to construct a new pilot fuel enrichment plant (Fordow, near Qom); construction since second half of 2007 per Iran
Enrichment to near 20% begins: LEU fed into one PFEP cascade on the evening of 9 Feb 2010; Iran reports up to 19.8% U-235 obtained 9-11 Feb 2010
First 20% product withdrawn at PFEP: 5.7 kg UF6, 19.7% U-235 according to Iran
First larger IR-2m cascade fed: Iran informed the Agency (letter 22 Jun 2011) it started feeding 54 IR-2m in PFEP Cascade 5 (136 installed by 28 Aug 2011)
First centrifuges at Fordow: one cascade designated for 20% production installed

GOV/2011/65 Annex on possible military dimensions: the Agency finds the information, overall, credible, that Iran carried out activities relevant to the development of a nuclear explosive device, under a structured programme before the end of 2003, and that some activities may still be ongoing
Fordow enrichment starts: UF6 enriched up to 5% fed into one set of two interconnected cascades (348 IR-1) in Unit 2 at FFEP, for up to 20%
First conversion of UF6 enriched up to 20% into U3O8 (for TRR fuel), at UCF/FPFP Esfahan
First centrifuges more advanced than the IR-1 installed at Natanz FEP (IR-2m; not fed with UF6 in 2013-2015)
IR-6 and IR-6s first installed at PFEP and intermittently fed with natural UF6 as single machines (GOV/2012/55 had reported only two empty IR-6 casings on 6 Nov 2012)
IR-5 installed at PFEP for the first time (single machine, not fed; still 'in place but without connections' in 2015)
New centrifuge casing Iran calls 'IR-8' observed at PFEP, not connected (Iran's DIQ of 4 Dec 2013 announced it)

Joint Plan of Action takes effect: Agency confirms Iran has ceased enriching above 5% at the two PFEP cascades and four FFEP cascades used for 20% production, stopped interconnected cascades, and begun diluting UF6 enriched up to 20% (the rest converted to oxide); detailed in GOV/2014/10 paras 18, 28, 32, 35

Downblending completed; all UF6 enriched up to 20% downblended or converted to oxide, apart from 0.6 kg kept as mass-spectrometry reference material (20% UF6 stock effectively zero). First GOV/ quarterly report to record it; a monthly JPA update (GOV/INF/2014/19 or later, not read) may have recorded it earlier

Final assessment of past and present outstanding issues (possible military dimensions): 'a range of activities relevant to the development of a nuclear explosive device were conducted in Iran prior to the end of 2003 as a coordinated effort, and some activities took place after 2003', they 'did not advance beyond feasibility and scientific studies', the Agency 'has no credible indications of activities ... relevant to the development of a nuclear explosive device after 2009', and found 'no credible indications of the diversion of nuclear material' in connection with them

Implementation Day verified: no more than 300 kg UF6 enriched up to 3.67% (excess downblended or sold and delivered out of Iran), no more than 5060 IR-1 at FEP and 1044 at Fordow, no enrichment at Fordow, all IR-2m removed to storage
IAEA verifies Iran's enriched uranium stock (205.0 kg U up to 3.67%) exceeds the JCPOA limit of 300 kg UF6 (202.8 kg U)
IAEA verifies, with on-line enrichment monitors, that Iran is enriching UF6 above 3.67% U-235 at Natanz FEP (operator: 'about 4.5%')

IAEA verifies that small cascades of advanced centrifuges at PFEP (20 IR-4, 10 IR-6, 20 IR-6) are accumulating, or prepared to accumulate, enriched uranium (no accumulation was allowed under the JCPOA)
First full-size advanced-centrifuge cascades accumulating enriched uranium: 164 IR-4 (R&D line 4) and 164 IR-2m (R&D line 5) at Natanz PFEP
Cascade of 30 IR-6 centrifuges at Natanz PFEP (R&D line 6) accumulating enriched uranium
Natural UF6 cylinder moved from Natanz to Fordow FFEP and connected to two IR-1 cascades in preparation for feeding (first nuclear material at Fordow since Implementation Day)
Iran resumes uranium enrichment at Fordow FFEP: UF6 fed into two IR-1 cascades (nuclear material present from 6 Nov 2019)
First cascade of advanced centrifuges (IR-2m, moved from PFEP) installed at Natanz FEP; on 9 Nov 2020 connected but not yet fed with UF6
First advanced-centrifuge cascade enriching at Natanz FEP: UF6 fed into a cascade of 174 IR-2m (installed 11 Oct 2020)

Enrichment up to 20% U-235 begins at Fordow: Agency inspectors confirm the six IR-1 cascades (1044 centrifuges) reconfigured as three sets of two interconnected cascades; Iran connects a cylinder of 137.2 kg U of UF6 enriched up to 4.1% to start producing up to 20% (also GOV/2021/10, para 24)

First uranium metal: 3.6 g produced from 13 g of natural UF4 in a laboratory experiment at FPFP, Esfahan, on 6 Feb 2021 (verified 8 Feb 2021). Later: 2.42 kg of natural uranium metal by 18 May 2021 (GOV/2021/28, para 28); 200 g of uranium metal enriched up to 20% by 14 Aug 2021 (GOV/2021/39, para 44); also GOV/2021/10, para 28

Last date on which the Agency verified Iran's total enriched uranium stockpile; from then on the quarterly figures are Agency estimates ('For this reporting period, the Agency has not been able to verify Iran's total enriched uranium stockpile')

Enrichment up to 60% U-235 begins at PFEP Natanz: up-to-5% UF6 fed simultaneously into IR-4 and IR-6 cascades in R&D lines 4 and 6; Iran declared 55.3%. Environmental samples of 22 Apr 2021 showed up to 63% U-235 (GOV/INF/2021/29, para 7)
First IR-6 cascade fed at Fordow: cascade of 166 IR-6 (fixed configuration) fed with up-to-5% UF6 to make up-to-20% (verified November 2021; first reported in GOV/2021/46, para. 5, not downloaded)

Iran has all JCPOA surveillance and monitoring equipment removed (9-11 June 2022; GOV/2022/39 para 7). Loss of continuity of knowledge: the Agency first states it 'would not be able to re-establish continuity of knowledge in relation to the production and inventory of centrifuges, rotors and bellows, heavy water and UOC' in GOV/2023/8 (para 11); later reports say it 'has lost' it (e.g. GOV/2024/61 para 30; GOV/2025/50 para 7).

Agency verifies production of UF6 enriched up to 60% at Fordow (two IR-6 cascades interconnected, fed with up-to-5% UF6); production since 21 Nov 2022. First reported in GOV/INF/2022/24, para. 9 (not downloaded).
Environmental samples taken at Fordow's product sampling point show HEU particles containing up to 83.7% U-235

Board of Governors resolution GOV/2025/38 finds that Iran's many failures to uphold its obligations constitute non-compliance with its Safeguards Agreement and that the Agency cannot verify that there has been no diversion of nuclear material. Rests on the comprehensive report GOV/2025/25 (31 May 2025), whose conclusions are in paras 77-86 (para 83: Iran did not declare nuclear material and activities at Lavisan-Shian, Varamin and Turquzabad).

Israeli military attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities begin (13-24 June 2025), the United States later participating; Agency stops verification and later withdraws all inspectors. Affected facilities with nuclear material: FFEP, FEP, PFEP, UCF (incl. uranium metal area), FMP, FPFP, EUPP.

Agency says it cannot quantify the enriched uranium stockpile with the same confidence and accuracy as before or determine its whereabouts (last estimate as of 13 June 2025: 9874.9 kg U, of which 440.9 kg U up to 60%)
Agency reports it lost continuity of knowledge on the current inventories of nuclear material, including LEU and HEU, during the reporting period after the attacks

First report saying the Agency 'cannot provide any information on the current size, composition or whereabouts of the stockpile of enriched uranium in Iran' (earlier, GOV/2025/50 para 34, Sep 2025: not in a position to quantify it with the same confidence or determine its whereabouts)
Further US and Israeli military attacks on Iran, including on sites of nuclear facilities; Agency again stops verification
